claim: Nanobodies (Nbs) are the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in camelids.
source: Nbs, the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in camelids (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993) and cartilaginous fishes (Greenberg et al., 1995), bind their cognate antigens with high affinity and specificity
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993

claim: Nanobodies (Nbs) are the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in cartilaginous fishes.
source: Nbs, the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in camelids (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993) and cartilaginous fishes (Greenberg et al., 1995), bind their cognate antigens with high affinity and specificity
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Greenberg et al., 1995

claim: Nanobodies bind their cognate antigens with high affinity and specificity.
source: Nbs, the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in camelids (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993) and cartilaginous fishes (Greenberg et al., 1995), bind their cognate antigens with high affinity and specificity
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about nanobodies and citations

claim: Nanobodies are very stable in the intracellular environment.
source: Nbs, the antigen recognition portions of single chain antibodies found in camelids (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993) and cartilaginous fishes (Greenberg et al., 1995), bind their cognate antigens with high affinity and specificity, and have the added advantage over heterotetrameric antibodies in that they are very stable in the intracellular environment.
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about nanobodies

claim: Fusions between Nbs and proteins with desirable activities have enabled a number of applications in living cells.
source: Fusions between Nbs and proteins with desirable activities have enabled a number of applications in living cells (Caussinus et al., 2012; Irannejad et al., 2013; Kirchhofer et al., 2010; Rothbauer et al., 2006; Tang et al., 2013, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work

claim: Genetically expressed Nb-fusion proteins are stable and active even in cells that do not express the cognate antigens.
source: Despite these successes, it has been difficult to take advantage of Nbs for live cell applications requiring cell-specificity, as genetically expressed Nb-fusion proteins are stable and active even in cells that do not express the cognate antigens.
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the problem statement in the introduction

claim: A destabilized GBP1 (dGBP1) variant carrying 6 amino acid changes (A25V, E63V, S73R, S98Y, Q109H, S117F) gave little to no TagBFP fluorescence with no signs of aggregation in the absence of YFP.
source: Notably, a GBP1 variant carrying 6 amino acid changes (A25V, E63V, S73R, S98Y, Q109H, S117F) gave little to no TagBFP fluorescence, with no signs of aggregation in the absence of YFP.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text

claim: dGBP1-TagBFP showed strong fluorescence and protein level when co-expressed with GFP or YFP.
source: dGBP1-TagBFP showed strong fluorescence and protein level when co-expressed with GFP or YFP, but became weakly detectable or undetectable when antigen was absent (Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D, E and supplementary figures

claim: dGBP1-TagBFP became weakly detectable or undetectable when antigen was absent.
source: dGBP1-TagBFP showed strong fluorescence and protein level when co-expressed with GFP or YFP, but became weakly detectable or undetectable when antigen was absent (Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D, E and supplementary figures

claim: Unmodified GBP1-TagBFP showed strong fluorescence and protein level regardless of antigen co-expression.
source: In contrast, unmodified GBP1-TagBFP showed strong fluorescence and protein level regardless of antigen co-expression (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D, E

claim: The level of wildtype GBP1-TagBFP protein increased in the presence of YFP.
source: Interestingly, we detected an increase in the level of wildtype GBP1-TagBFP protein in the presence of YFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: dGBP1-TagBFP fluorescence and protein level were detected only upon GFP co-expression in vivo in the mouse retina.
source: In an electroporation experiment using the mouse retina, dGBP1-TagBFP fluorescence and protein level were detected only upon GFP co-expression in vivo (Figure 1F–H, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from in vivo electroporation experiments shown in figures

claim: The efficiency of TagBFP stabilization by GFP expression was nearly 100% in electroporated retinal cells.
source: Strikingly, the efficiency of TagBFP stabilization by GFP expression was nearly 100%, i.e. almost every GFP+ cell was TagBFP+ (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The efficiency of the TDDOG and CRE-DOG systems was, at the highest, ~60% in similarly designed electroporation experiments.
source: The efficiency of the TDDOG and CRE-DOG systems was, at the highest, ~60% in similarly designed electroporation experiments (Tang et al., 2013, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work by Tang et al.

claim: YFP promoted dGBP1-TagBFP stability in a dose-dependent manner, with no adverse effects even when YFP plasmid was transfected at ten-fold excess of dGBP1-TagBFP plasmid.
source: Indeed, YFP promoted dGBP1-TagBFP stability in a dose-dependent manner, with no adverse effects even when YFP plasmid was transfected at ten-fold excess of dGBP1-TagBFP plasmid (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 1I

claim: dGBP1-TagBFP protein was degraded by the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS).
source: dGBP1-TagBFP protein was evident following addition of either inhibitor and was absent without inhibitors, indicating that it was degraded by the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteasome inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 1J

claim: C/S98Y and S117F showed strong destabilizing effects in GBP1.
source: C/S98Y and S117F showed strong destabilizing effects, as seen in both sufficiency and necessity experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by mutational analysis data described in the text and shown in supplementary figures

claim: S73R and Q109H had destabilizing effects in single mutant analyses of GBP1.
source: S73R and Q109H also had destabilizing effects in single mutant analyses.
evidence: The claim is supported by mutational analysis data

claim: GFP rescued the destabilization phenotype of all GBP1 mutants.
source: GFP rescued the destabilization phenotype of all mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations from mutational analysis

claim: The dGBP1 mutations mapped onto the structurally conserved framework regions of Nbs.
source: The dGBP1 mutations mapped onto the structurally conserved framework regions of Nbs (Muyldermans, 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis and citation

claim: 99–100% of Nbs (n=76) shared the same residue as GBP1 at each of the 3 most destabilizing positions (3maj: S73R, C/S98Y, S117F).
source: 99–100% of Nbs (n=76) shared the same residue as GBP1 at each of the 3 most destabilizing positions (3maj: S73R, C/S98Y, S117F) (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence conservation analysis shown in figures

claim: Nb positions corresponding to dGBP1 A25V, S73R, S98Y and S117F were universally located outside of all Nb-antigen interfaces across 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces.
source: a survey across 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces, gathered from a total of 102 crystal structures, indicated that Nb positions corresponding to those of dGBP1 A25V, S73R, S98Y and S117F were universally located outside of all Nb-antigen interfaces (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of crystal structures shown in supplementary figures

claim: Nb positions corresponding to dGBP1 Q109H fell outside of 99%, or 75 of 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces.
source: Nb positions corresponding to dGBP1 Q109H fell outside of 99%, or 75 of 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of crystal structures

claim: Positions equivalent to dGBP1 E63V were found in 22%, or 17 of 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces.
source: Positions equivalent to dGBP1 E63V were found in 22%, or 17 of 76 unique Nb-antigen interfaces, and in close proximity to the interface in 9%, or 7 of 76 of the cases.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of crystal structures

claim: dNbs created by mutation transfer of dGBP1 mutations to αCA and αDHFR Nbs showed antigen-dependent TagBFP fusion fluorescence and protein level.
source: dNbs created by mutation transfer behaved similarly as dGBP1 in that TagBFP fusion fluorescence and protein level both depended upon expression of the cognate antigen (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-E

claim: Destabilization of dNbs created by mutation transfer depended on degradation by the UPS.
source: Destabilization also depended on degradation by the UPS (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteasome inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 2F

claim: dGBP1-TagBFP did not have an obvious effect on YFP protein level when compared to the negative control condition.
source: Using western blots to quantify protein levels, we found that dGBP1-TagBFP did not have an obvious effect on YFP protein level, when compared to the negative control condition whereby αCA6mut-TagBFP replaced dGBP1-TagBFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C

claim: 8 of 9, or 89% of dNbs generated by mutation transfer showed >2 fold increase in TagBFP fluorescence in response to antigen co-expression.
source: Importantly, whereas no unmodified Nb showed >2 fold increase in TagBFP fluorescence in response to antigen co-expression, 8 of 9, or 89% of dNbs, passed this threshold (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative fluorescence data shown in Figure 2G

claim: Mutations that destabilized a Camelus dromedarius Nb (GBP1) had very similar effects on Nbs derived from Vicugna pacos and Llama glama.
source: Notably, mutations that destabilized a Camelus dromedarius Nb (GBP1) had very similar effects on Nbs derived from Vicugna pacos and Llama glama, indicating that destabilizing mutations can be transferred across Nbs from different camelid species to create antigen-dependence (Figure 2A and G; Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, G and Table 1

claim: Cre and codon-optimized Flp (Flpo) were rendered GFP-dependent after fusion to dGBP1, but not GBP1.
source: Both enzymes were rendered GFP-dependent after fusion to dGBP1, but not GBP1 (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3A-B

claim: Increasing the number of dGBP1 domains fused to Cre or Flpo decreased residual GFP-independent recombination without affecting GFP-dependent recombination.
source: By increasing the number of dGBP1 domains fused to either enzyme, residual GFP-independent recombination of the initial fusions was decreased without affecting GFP-dependent recombination (Figure 3A–B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in figures

claim: Flpo fused to tandemly repeated dGBP1 (dGBP1x2-Flpo, or Flp-DOG) had insignificant background signal and over 600 fold induction by GFP.
source: Notably, Flpo fused to tandemly repeated dGBP1 (dGBP1x2-Flpo, or Flp dependent on GFP [Flp-DOG]) had insignificant background signal and over 600 fold induction by GFP (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3B

claim: An Flpo fusion protein dependent upon the C-terminal portion of HIV-1 CA (C-CA) was functional in vitro and in vivo.
source: We also rapidly constructed an Flpo fusion protein dependent upon the C-terminal portion of HIV-1 CA (C-CA) using mutation transfer. This construct was functional in vitro and in vivo(Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and supplementary figures

claim: Both GFP- and C-CA-dependent Flpo responded to antigen in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Further, both GFP- and C-CA-dependent Flpo responded to antigen in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Flpo fused to dGBP1 and αCA dNb6mut (dGC-Flpo) or dGBP1 and αDHFR dNb3maj (dGD-Flpo) showed strong recombination only when both antigens were present.
source: Strong Flpo recombination was triggered only when both antigens were present (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by dual antigen experiments shown in Figure 3D-E

claim: Co-expression of C-CA with dCC-Cas9 and loxPgRNA triggered genome-editing events in a human cell line.
source: Co-expression of C-CA with dCC-Cas9 and loxPgRNA triggered genome-editing events, while little to no β-galactosidase expression was detected when C-CA was absent (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by genome editing assay data shown in Figure 4D

claim: The efficiency of C-CA-dependent genome editing approached that of control Cas9.
source: The efficiency of C-CA-dependent genome editing approached that of control Cas9 (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by genome editing efficiency data shown in Figure 4D

claim: Robust Flpo recombination was detected in GFP+ tissues of Tg(CRX-GFP) and Tg(GAD67-GFP) mice after delivery of Flp-DOG.
source: In both instances, robust Flpo recombination was detected in GFP+ tissues, but not in GFP-negative tissues labeled with electroporation, infection or injection markers (Figure 5A–C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo recombination data shown in figures

claim: Flpo recombination was not detected in GFP-negative tissues labeled with electroporation, infection or injection markers.
source: In both instances, robust Flpo recombination was detected in GFP+ tissues, but not in GFP-negative tissues labeled with electroporation, infection or injection markers (Figure 5A–C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo recombination data shown in figures

claim: Excitatory photocurrents and synaptic inhibitory currents were evoked in ChR2-mCherry+ Purkinje cells of Tg(GAD67-GFP) cerebella.
source: Under conditions in which infection did not alter spontaneous firing frequency or input resistance, we evoked excitatory photocurrents and synaptic inhibitory currents in ChR2-mCherry+ PCs, with inhibitory inputs from neighboring ChR2-mCherry+ neurons that contacted the recorded PCs (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 2F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5 and supplementary figures

claim: GFP+ neurons that did not express ChR2-mCherry never showed light-evoked photocurrents.
source: GFP+ neurons that did not express ChR2-mCherry, as well as control ZsGreen+ neurons in GFP-negative animals, never showed light-evoked photocurrents, indicating antigen-specificity of the system (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Control ZsGreen+ neurons in GFP-negative animals never showed light-evoked photocurrents.
source: GFP+ neurons that did not express ChR2-mCherry, as well as control ZsGreen+ neurons in GFP-negative animals, never showed light-evoked photocurrents, indicating antigen-specificity of the system (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Destabilized αCA fused to TagBFP or TagRFP were expressed in ACH-2 and CEM cell lines under conditions in which HIV-1 was reactivated with PMA.
source: Destabilized αCA fused to either TagBFP or TagRFP (Matz et al., 1999) were expressed in ACH-2 or the uninfected parental cell line (CEM), under conditions in which HIV-1 was reactivated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) (Poli et al., 1990) (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental description and citations

claim: Fluorescence of destabilized αCA-TagBFP fusions was detected selectively in ACH-2, but not CEM cells by flow cytometry.
source: Using flow cytometry, we detected fluorescence of the destabilized fusions selectively in ACH-2, but not CEM cells (Figure 6B–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B-C and supplementary figures

claim: ACH-2-specific fluorescence was dependent upon CA recognition, as the effect was not observed with dGBP1-TagBFP.
source: ACH-2-specific fluorescence was dependent upon CA recognition, as the effect was not observed with dGBP1-TagBFP.
evidence: The claim is supported by negative control experiments with dGBP1-TagBFP

claim: Unmodified αCA Nb-TagBFP fluoresced strongly in both ACH-2 and CEM cell lines and could not be used to distinguish between the two.
source: Importantly, unmodified αCA Nb-TagBFP fluoresced strongly in both cell lines and could not be used to distinguish between the two (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B-C

claim: HIV-1 CA antigen was specifically detected by immunofluorescence in ACH-2, but not CEM cells.
source: we confirmed that αCA dNb6mut-TagBFP could be stabilized by C-CA co-expression in CEM cells (data not shown) and that the HIV-1 CA antigen was specifically detected by immunofluorescence in ACH-2, but not CEM cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C

claim: The screening strategy described should enable the creation of additional protein-responsive reagents useful for control of fusion protein activity in specific cell populations.
source: The screening strategy described here should enable the creation of additional protein-responsive reagents useful for control of fusion protein activity in specific cell populations.
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement based on the demonstrated success of the screening strategy

claim: The screening strategy can be extended to generate a diversity of protein-responsive, destabilized binders based on the Nb scaffold or other protein scaffolds.
source: In principle, this screening strategy can be extended to generate a diversity of protein-responsive, destabilized binders based on the Nb scaffold or other protein scaffolds (Wurch et al., 2012; Helma et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement based on the principles demonstrated and supported by citations

claim: All successfully modified Nbs were derived from camelid species different from that of GBP1.
source: All successfully modified Nbs were derived from camelid species different from that of GBP1, demonstrating the broad transferability of the mutations discovered here.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data showing mutation transfer across species

claim: The efficiency of the GFP/dGBP1 system was nearly 100% in electroporated cells of the retina.
source: Indeed, we observed that the most direct output of the GFP/dGBP1 system – a dGBP1 fusion protein (dGBP1-TagBFP), could be stabilized by YFP with close to 100% efficiency amongst electroporated cells of the retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and C

claim: The activity of Flp-DOG continued to rise along with increasing GFP levels.
source: Also, whereas the previous dimerizer-based systems were inhibited by excessive amounts of GFP, the activity of Flp-DOG continued to rise along with increasing GFP levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) (Tang et al., 2015, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and comparison to prior work

claim: It was necessary to remove the woodchuck hepatitis virus post-transcriptional regulatory element (WPRE) sequence from the rAAV expression cassette in order to avoid background Flp-DOG activity with rAAV infection.
source: Indeed, we found that it was necessary to remove the woodchuck hepatitis virus post-transcriptional regulatory element (WPRE) sequence from the rAAV expression cassette in order to avoid background Flp-DOG activity with rAAV infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations during optimization

claim: Tandemly repeated dGBP1s were fused to Flpo in order obtain tight GFP-dependent recombination.
source: Second, tandemly repeated dGBP1s were fused to Flpo in order obtain tight GFP-dependent recombination.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental design described

claim: Flp-DOG had adequate activity for the targeting of GFP cell types of the two different transgenic GFP lines tested.
source: However, in practice, Flp-DOG had adequate activity for the targeting of GFP cell types of the two different transgenic GFP lines tested.
evidence: The claim is supported by the in vivo experimental results in transgenic mice

claim: Endogenous proteins should be usable as driver molecules to trigger sensor or effector activity.
source: Beyond fluorescent proteins, endogenous proteins should be usable as driver molecules to trigger sensor or effector activity.
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement based on the principles demonstrated

claim: Using endogenous proteins as driver molecules would enable one to selectively target specific cell types in wildtype animals for experimentation, without requiring any knowledge of cell type-specific promoters or creation of knock-in alleles.
source: Endogenous proteins would enable one to selectively target specific cell types in wildtype animals for experimentation, without requiring any knowledge of cell type-specific promoters or creation of knock-in alleles.
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement about potential applications

claim: Background signals of dNb fusion proteins could be addressed by simply increasing the number of dNbs fused to the protein partner.
source: Background signals could be addressed by simply increasing the number of dNbs fused to the protein partner.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results showing reduced background with tandem dNbs

claim: Background activity of dGBP1-Cre could be further controlled by fusion to an ERT2 domain to create small-molecule dependency.
source: For example, background activity of dGBP1-Cre could be further controlled by fusion to an ERT2 domain to create small-molecule dependency (Feil et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is a suggestion for future optimization supported by citation

claim: The fusion of protein binders to fluorescent proteins enables visualization of antigen localization in living cells.
source: The fusion of protein binders to fluorescent proteins enables visualization of antigen localization in living cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about protein binder-fluorescent protein fusions

claim: A dNb-TagBFP construct became strictly localized to the nucleus upon co-expression with its NLS-tagged antigen.
source: Indeed, we found that a dNb-TagBFP construct became strictly localized to the nucleus upon co-expression with its NLS-tagged antigen (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations mentioned in the text

claim: Dual antigen dependence may enable one to precisely target specific cell populations in ways similar to established intersectional strategies, but using proteins that do not necessarily have any defined regulatory abilities.
source: With further development, dual antigen dependence may enable one to precisely target specific cell populations in ways similar to established intersectional strategies, but using proteins that do not necessarily have any defined regulatory abilities (Dymecki et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement about potential applications supported by citations

claim: The strategy wherein dNb-Cas9 activity is suppressed until antigen can stabilize the fusion protein offers a novel strategy to restrict the cell populations that might suffer from off-targeting events.
source: The strategy developed here, wherein dNb-Cas9 activity is suppressed until antigen can stabilize the fusion protein, offers a novel strategy to restrict the cell populations that might suffer from off-targeting events.
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement about potential applications

claim: Over the past 20 years, ~100 crystal structures featuring Nb-antigen complexes have been solved.
source: Over the past 20 years, ~100 crystal structures featuring Nb-antigen complexes have been solved.
evidence: The claim is supported by the structural database analysis described in methods

claim: Multiple classes of artificially derived binding proteins that are amenable to expression in living cells are being developed for antigen-recognition.
source: Beyond Nbs, multiple classes of artificially derived binding proteins that are amenable to expression in living cells are being developed for antigen-recognition (Helma et al., 2015; Wurch et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to the literature

claim: It should be possible to generate epitope-responsive properties by incorporating a common set of mutations onto conserved and non-epitope binding regions of protein binder scaffolds.
source: As epitope-specific binders are typically generated by varying loops or surfaces on a common structural scaffold, it should be possible to generate epitope-responsive properties by incorporating a common set of mutations onto conserved and non-epitope binding regions of the scaffold.
evidence: The claim is a forward-looking statement based on the principles demonstrated with Nbs

claim: GBP1 was used for proof-of-concept experiments to test whether it is possible to modify an Nb such that its intracellular protein level is strongly dependent upon antigen co-expression.
source: To test whether it is possible to modify an Nb such that its intracellular protein level is strongly dependent upon antigen co-expression, we used the GFP-binding Nb, GBP1, for proof-of-concept experiments (Kirchhofer et al., 2010; Rothbauer et al., 2006) (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental design described and citations

claim: A Moloney murine leukemia virus (MMLV) library encoding randomly mutagenized variants of GBP1 fused to TagBFP was generated.
source: We generated a Moloney murine leukemia virus (MMLV) library encoding randomly mutagenized variants of GBP1 fused to the blue fluorescent protein, TagBFP (Subach et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description and citation

claim: t-HcRed was co-expressed via an IRES to report infection in the MMLV library screen.
source: t-HcRed (Gurskaya et al., 2001) was co-expressed via an IRES to report infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description and citation

claim: TagBFP and t-HcRed bear little amino acid similarity to Aequorea-derived GFP and its derivatives.
source: TagBFP and t-HcRed bear little amino acid similarity to Aequorea-derived GFP and its derivatives.
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about these fluorescent proteins

claim: 293T cells were infected with the MMLV library and FACS was combined with super-infection by a GFP-encoding rAAV to isolate GBP1-TagBFP variants whose blue fluorescence depended upon GFP expression.
source: We infected 293T cells with this library, and combined FACS with super-infection by a GFP-encoding recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) to isolate GBP1-TagBFP variants whose blue fluorescence depended upon GFP expression (Figure 1B; Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by the screening strategy description

claim: One hundred GBP1 variants were individually screened for enhanced TagBFP expression in the presence of YFP.
source: One hundred GBP1 variants were then individually screened for enhanced TagBFP expression in the presence of yellow fluorescent protein (YFP), a GFP derivative known to also interact with GBP1 (Rothbauer et al., 2008; Tang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by the screening strategy description and citations

claim: Some GBP1 variants showed fusion TagBFP aggregates within well-transfected cells when YFP was absent, but became soluble in the cytoplasm when YFP was present.
source: Some variants showed fusion TagBFP aggregates within well-transfected cells when YFP was absent, but became soluble in the cytoplasm when YFP was present (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Virtually all MMLV-infected cells in culture can be super-infected by rAAV, and the cells remain viable for subsequent culture expansion and FACS.
source: A key feature of our screen is the use of rAAVs to deliver the antigen to cells. Virtually all MMLV-infected cells in culture can be super-infected by rAAV, and the cells remain viable for subsequent culture expansion and FACS.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations during screening

claim: Flp-DOG provides a much simpler approach to manipulate GFP-defined cell types over pre-existing methods.
source: Thus, Flp-DOG provides a much simpler approach to manipulate GFP-defined cell types over pre-existing methods.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to prior methods requiring multiple components

claim: dNb-fusion proteins enable functional manipulation of antigen-expressing cells in vivo.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate that dNb-fusion proteins enable functional manipulation of antigen-expressing cells in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by the in vivo experimental results in mice

claim: dNbs make possible detection of intracellular viral epitopes without the need for cell fixation or membrane permeabilization.
source: Thus, dNbs make possible detection of intracellular viral epitopes without the need for cell fixation or membrane permeabilization, enabling live monitoring of intracellular viral protein expression and specific isolation of infected live cells with a choice of spectrally distinct fluorescent proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by the HIV-1 detection experiments using flow cytometry

claim: dNbs enable live monitoring of intracellular viral protein expression and specific isolation of infected live cells with a choice of spectrally distinct fluorescent proteins.
source: Thus, dNbs make possible detection of intracellular viral epitopes without the need for cell fixation or membrane permeabilization, enabling live monitoring of intracellular viral protein expression and specific isolation of infected live cells with a choice of spectrally distinct fluorescent proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by the HIV-1 detection experiments using flow cytometry with different fluorescent proteins

claim: The Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Harvard University approved all animal experiments.
source: The Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at Harvard University approved all animal experiments.
evidence: The claim is a statement of regulatory compliance

claim: Timed pregnant CD1 mice were used for electroporation experiments.
source: Timed pregnant CD1 (Charles River Breeding Laboratories, Boston, MA) were used for electroporation experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description

claim: Tg(CRX-GFP) and Tg(GAD67-GFP) mice were kept on a C57/BL6J background.
source: Tg(CRX-GFP) (Samson et al., 2009) and Tg(GAD67-GFP) (Tamamaki et al., 2003) were kept on a C57/BL6J background.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description and citations

claim: Between 9,000–160,000 colonies were produced per library preparation in the MMLV mutagenesis library.
source: Between 9,000–160,000 colonies were produced per library preparation, with 85% of sequenced colonies carrying a unique combination of GBP1 mutations.
evidence: The claim is supported by the library generation data described in methods

claim: 85% of sequenced colonies in the MMLV mutagenesis library carried a unique combination of GBP1 mutations.
source: Between 9,000–160,000 colonies were produced per library preparation, with 85% of sequenced colonies carrying a unique combination of GBP1 mutations.
evidence: The claim is supported by the library generation data described in methods

claim: rAAV (2/1) virus preparations were made from pAAV-EF1α-dGBP1x2-Flpo-NW and pAAV-CAG-FLEXFRT-ChR2-mCherry.
source: rAAV (2/1) virus preparations were made from pAAV-EF1α-dGBP1x2-Flpo-NW and pAAV-CAG-FLEXFRT-ChR2-mCherry.
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description

claim: All rAAVs were injected in the range of 1013–1014 genome copies/ml.
source: All rAAVs were injected in the range of 1013–1014 genome copies/ml, assayed by PCR of rAAV vectors at Boston Children's Hospital (Zhigang He lab).
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description

claim: ACH-2 is a human T-cell line chronically infected with HIV-1.
